text: Why does doubling give amortized constant time per add?
choices: Because copying is faster than allocating
Because the JIT removes the copies
Because each add copies only one element
The total copying over n additions is 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + n/2, which is less than n
explanation: Fewer than n copies in total for n additions, so each one costs a constant amount on average even though individual adds occasionally copy a great deal. Growing by a fixed 100 instead would cost about five billion copies for a million items.
